primitives.name: Decoy Call Signaling
primitives.verbatim_quote: 140 AMERICAN FOOTBALL they must call for the ball by shouting or by such other outward manifestations as the situation may demand and as are calculated to mislead the defense.
primitives.assumptions: Players must use audible shouts or non-verbal signals to indicate target receiver intent.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when defenders intercept the signal, causing miscommunication and disrupted plays.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Signal-to-noise ratio determines optimal decoy selection. GSE: Actionable telemetry tracks defender reaction times to identify successful calls.
layer2.telemetry: Defender response time variance to player signals.

primitives.name: Decoy Training Discipline
primitives.verbatim_quote: A coach cannot be too particular about training players in their work as decoys.
primitives.assumptions: Coaches enforce strict behavioral protocols to prevent defenders from distinguishing between genuine receivers and decoys.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Training gaps lead to predictable patterns that defenders exploit, undermining play design.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Decoys are treated as distinct probabilistic classes requiring separate inference models. GSE: State transitions track whether decoys successfully hold defensive positions.
layer2.telemetry: Decoy positioning accuracy relative to defensive alignment metrics.

primitives.name: Protection by Blocking
primitives.verbatim_quote: PROTECTION AND DELAY Protection and delay may be obtained either by the line and backs blocking fast all opponents charging the passer or by deception.
primitives.assumptions: The offensive line and running backs form a physical barrier to protect the quarterback during the throw.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Blocking breaks down when defenders penetrate the wall faster than the two-second throw window.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Models blocking efficiency as a conformal prediction set for defender arrival times. GSE: Tracks the spatial-temporal state of blockers to ensure continuous coverage.
layer2.telemetry: Average distance defenders travel toward quarterback per second.

primitives.name: Surprise Element
primitives.verbatim_quote: If the element of surprise is properly handled by the quarterback and the pass is thrown from a quick lineup, this delay and protection are readily obtained.
primitives.assumptions: Quick pre-snap movement and unpredictable handoffs create uncertainty in defender expectations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Surprise fails when defenders anticipate the motion, reducing the effective delay window.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Surprise is modeled as a prior distribution shift that increases receiver success probability. GSE: The quarterback's micro-movements serve as state variables triggering specific receiver routes.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation between quarterback cadence speed and receiver catch rate.
